question_text: Find the derivative of tan⁻¹((√(1 + x²) − 1)/x).

mark_split.label: Put x = tan θ and reduce the fraction to tan(θ/2)

steps.label: Put x = tan θ and reduce the fraction to tan(θ/2)
steps.margin_note: First mark, and the step the rest of the answer depends on. √(1 + x²) is what makes x = tan θ the right substitution: 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, so the root becomes sec θ and the fraction becomes (1 − cos θ)/sin θ, which is the half-angle form of tan(θ/2).
steps.memory_tip: A √(1 + x²) inside an inverse trigonometric function means the substitution x = tan θ, because 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ removes the root.
lines: Put x = tan θ, so θ = Tan⁻¹x,
(put √(1 + x²) = sec θ and x = tan θ)
(multiply the top and the bottom by cos θ)

recall.must_convey: That x = tan θ makes √(1 + x²) equal to sec θ, and the fraction reduces to (1 − cos θ)/sin θ = tan(θ/2).

steps.why: Differentiating the printed expression with the quotient and chain rules takes several lines and rarely simplifies by hand. The substitution replaces it by a single half-angle in one move, which is why this line carries the method mark.
common_mistakes: Substituting x = sin θ, which leaves √(1 + sin²θ) and does not simplify.
Writing √(sec²θ) as ±sec θ and losing the sign, when sec θ is positive throughout (−π/2, π/2).

steps.label: Differentiate half the inverse tangent
steps.margin_note: Second mark. θ/2 lies in (−π/4, π/4), inside the principal range of Tan⁻¹, so the inverse tangent cancels and y = (1/2)Tan⁻¹x. Only the constant 1/2 separates this from the standard derivative.
steps.memory_tip: y is half of Tan⁻¹x, so the answer is half the standard derivative 1/(1 + x²).

the answer is one over two into one plus x squared
tan inverse of tan theta by two is theta by two

half the standard tan inverse derivative

steps.why: The mark is for finishing with the standard derivative of Tan⁻¹x and keeping the 1/2. Do not lose the half.
common_mistakes: Writing 1/(1 + x²) and losing the factor 1/2 that came from θ/2.
Writing 1/(2 + x²) by putting the 2 inside the bracket instead of multiplying the whole denominator.

insider_note: x = tan θ makes the bracket (1 − cos θ)/sin θ, which is tan(θ/2) — so y = θ/2 and the answer is half the Tan⁻¹ derivative. Do not lose the ½.
